newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower after CPI data.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower after CPI data.

text.p: New York precious metals prices ended mostly lower Friday, continuing the decline of the past 12 days, with news of only a 0.1 percent rise in the August U.S. CPI Friday boosting U.S. equity and bond markets, and providing little incentive for investors to move into precious metals, analysts said.

"Given that the present economic picture in the U.S. and Japan is healthy, investment demand for precious metals is expected to remain fairly weak over the next few months," CPM Group's New York-based analyst Edward Kemp said.
COMEX December gold ended down 20 cents at $385.60 an ounce, after trading in a $385.50-386.70 range.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $382.20/382.70, compared to the London afternoon fix at $382.80, and the New York close Thursday at $382.45/382.95.

The IMF board meeting in Washington Friday is expected to reconsider the plan to sell about five million ounces of the IMF's reserve to help finance its third world debt relief plan, but any decision would likely be known after the market closed, analysts said.

"While the IMF's members have been discussing selling five million ounces of gold for the past five years and many in the market have discounted that these sales will be made over the next few years, recent comments suggesting this will indeed happen has led some proprietary traders and speculators to sell gold," Kempf said.
"Related to this was a story concerning old gold stolen by the Nazis in World War Two and held in Switzerland," he said.

"The idea that 17 million ounces of such gold may exist and somehow come onto the market roiled prices after the British Foreign Office released a historical brief on the subject Tuesday this week," he said.
COMEX December silver ended down 0.7 cent at $5.053, after trading in a $5.045-5.110 range.
Both gold and silver have drifted lower in the past three weeks, as fund selling and weak industrial demand brought an end to the July/August rally, analysts said.

But technical indicators suggest the precious metals complex has become oversold, and may find support again around $380 in spot gold, $5.00 in spot silver, $390 in spot platinum and $120 in spot palladium, analysts said.
NYMEX October platinum ended down $1.10 an ounce at $390.70, after seeing a fresh contract low at $389.60 early.
NYMEX December palladium ended up 30 cents at $123.95, but saw a life-of-contract low at $122.55 earlier this week.
